channel.title: DataCuse Stories & Notes
channel.description: Small discoveries, curious maps, and stories about Syracuse—one question at a time.

item.title: What's Syracuse's longest street—and where does it really end?
item.description: Canal Street goes the distance, one street name repeats itself, and South Salina wins after Erie Boulevard stops getting double credit.

item.title: How many names can a straight road have?
item.description: Monticello South becomes Monticello North, then Springbrook. A ruler test separates Syracuse's straight stretches from roads that merely keep going.

item.title: What's Syracuse's shortest street?
item.description: Two seven-letter names, one tiny lane, and a mapping wrinkle: Syracuse's shortest streets take us in three directions.

item.title: Are there oak trees on Oak Street?
item.description: Six oaks, 56 maples, and a spreadsheet investigation into whether Syracuse trees take street names literally.

item.title: Library use across Syracuse
item.description: Read the OCPL Library Use Story, with the underlying library dashboard as its source.

item.title: Below the Line 2026
item.description: How has poverty in Syracuse changed since the original 2018 report? Explore housing costs, work, education, transportation, and comparisons with other cities.

item.title: Connecting local data and library tools
item.description: Introducing DataCuse MCP: how one server brings together Syracuse open data, library tasks, and county, state, and federal sources.

item.title: Residents found a snow-plow workaround.
item.description: What happens when the service-request menu doesn't include the problem a resident needs to report? A look at snow-related requests in Cityline.
